A small round four-petalled clover character (tRNA) rides on its back, holding a big bead out with two petal-arms and trailing a small bead on a curly tail. prompt_v1_final:
A black-and-white children's coloring-book page, square 1:1, 1080x1080, drawn as an extreme close-up crop — like a photo taken so close to a big toy that the toy's own edges run straight off every side of the picture. The white paper of the page IS the picture; the linework itself is the only edge that exists.

SCENE: A long, cheerful RIBBON CHARACTER (Messenger RNA) stretches diagonally from the upper-left corner of the picture to the lower-right corner, like a big wavy scarf or noodle with a friendly face. Draw ONE happy round face partway along the ribbon's length (in the middle of the picture): two big round eyes with pupils, cheerful eyebrows, a wide open smile. The ribbon is drawn SO LONG that both of its ends run straight off the picture's edges — the upper-left end is cut off by the top edge and the left edge at once, and the lower-right end is cut off by the bottom edge and the right edge at once — pretend the picture was cropped in tight afterwards, exactly like a close-up photo of something too big to fit. Along the ribbon's length, draw a simple repeating pattern of small plain rounded notches (bumps) along both of its edges, evenly spaced, plain shapes with no writing on them. Partway along the ribbon, near the character's face, draw the ribbon folding back on itself in a simple, clear loop — like a shoelace loop or a bunny-ear loop — so it reads as a friendly little bow tucked into the ribbon's own length.

Riding on top of the ribbon, right next to the face, draw a SECOND, SMALLER, ROUND character: a cheerful four-petalled CLOVER-SHAPED character (Transfer RNA) with its own simple happy face in the middle of the four petals (two round eyes, a small smile) and two stubby little arms made from two of its petals, reaching out to hold a single big round BEAD between its "hands" as if it is proudly presenting it to the ribbon character. From the clover character's bottom petal, draw a short curly tail ending in a small plain round bead, bouncing along behind it.

In the lower-left area of the picture, partly cut off by the left edge and the bottom edge, draw a cluster of ROUND, BUMPY, KNOBBLY SHAPES pressed together like a pile of large soap bubbles or a cauliflower floret (a Ribosome) — one bigger rounded mass with a smaller rounded mass tucked against it, both made of many small overlapping bumps, with one small simple happy face peeking out from the bigger mass. Draw the ribbon character threading through a small gap between the two bumpy masses.

Fill any remaining open paper with a loose scatter of extra plain round beads and small plain circles of different sizes, several of them positioned right at the top, left, right and bottom edges so they too are cut off by the picture's border, leaving generous open white space inside every shape for a child to colour.

STYLE — coloring book line art:
- Bold, thick, even black outlines on pure white paper. Every shape a simple closed line.
- No shading, no grey tones, no hatching, no stippling, no gradients, no colour fill, no solid black fill anywhere except small solid pupils in the eyes.
- Simple, cheerful, chunky cartoon shapes with plenty of open white space for colouring.
- The picture fills the entire square canvas edge-to-edge on every side — every one of the four edges of the square has linework crossing it (the long ribbon, the bumpy ribosome cluster, or the scattered beads), so that no strip of empty paper margin runs along any edge.

Avoid: pointed rays, spikes, sparkle or starburst shapes of any kind; any rectangle, panel, ground-line, shelf or vignette drawn around the scene; any text, letters, numbers or captions; any speech bubble (added separately afterwards); a twisted double-helix ladder anywhere (the ribbon is a single flat strand, never two strands twisted together); human hands or arrows.
